newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Prosecutors summon S.Korean Kim's son over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors summon S.Korean Kim's son over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors have asked President Kim Young-sam's son to appear at their office on Friday for questioning in connection with massive loans to the failed Hanbo Steel Co, a prosecution official said on Thursday.
The prosecutors will question Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, over his libel complaint against six opposition politicians who accused him of peddling influence in giving the loans.
Kim Hyun-chul has said he had nothing to do with five trillion won ($5.8 billion) of loans that Hanbo Steel racked up before being declared insolvent on January 23.
Senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog told reporters that the prosecution would first focus on the libel complaint but also look into suspicions raised by opposition members.

State prosecutors on Wednesday indicted 10 people, including Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo and three close associates of President Kim, on charges of bribery and embezzlement in the loans for kick-back scandal. Hanbo Steel is the flagship of the Hanbo Group, South Korea's 14th-biggest conglomerate.
The main opposition National Congress for New Politics on Thursday lashed out at state prosecutors for what it called a "disappointing" investigation and called for a fresh prosecution probe.
